\paragraph{Spectral--Recurrence--Index Closure: The Verifiable Triangle of the Gauge Anomaly Mechanism}\label{par:fold-gauge-anomaly-spectral-recurrence-triangle}
The generated fragments input in the previous paragraph have already provided the pressure function of the per-bit gauge anomaly process (Proposition \ref{prop:fold-gauge-anomaly-pressure}), the Jordan correlation closed form (Theorem \ref{thm:fold-gauge-anomaly-autocov-closed}),
the spectral fingerprint and Hankel certificate (Theorem \ref{thm:fold-gauge-anomaly-hankel-rank3}), as well as the large deviation endpoints and algebraic rate curve (Proposition \ref{prop:fold-gauge-anomaly-ldp} and Proposition \ref{prop:fold-gauge-anomaly-rate-curve-param}).
This paragraph further compresses these results into three classes of \emph{finite-data verifiable} interfaces: the rational fingerprint of the frequency-domain power spectrum, the fourth-order closed recurrence of the finite-length moment generating function, and the finite index (maximal fiber multiplicity) of the folding conditional expectation.
\begin{theorem}[Jordan Spectral Fingerprint: Power Spectrum of the Per-Bit Gauge Anomaly Indicator Process Is a Rational Function]\label{thm:fold-gauge-anomaly-psd-rational}
Under the uniform baseline and stationary caliber of Proposition \ref{prop:fold-gauge-anomaly-pressure},
let \(g_t=\mathbf 1\{X_t\neq Y_t\}\in\{0,1\}\), and write
\(
C_k:=\mathrm{Cov}(g_t,g_{t+k})
\) (\(k\in\ZZ\)).
Define its discrete power spectrum (Fourier--Stieltjes transform)
\[
\mathcal S_g(\omega):=\sum_{k\in\ZZ} C_k e^{-ik\omega}\qquad(\omega\in\RR).
\]
Then \(\mathcal S_g\) is a strictly rational function; writing \(s:=e^{i\omega}\), the fully closed form is
\begin{equation}\label{eq:fold-gauge-anomaly-psd-rational}
\boxed{\;
\mathcal S_g(\omega)=\frac{2}{9}\cdot
\frac{4s^{6}+3s^{5}-46s^{4}-99s^{3}-46s^{2}+3s+4}{8s^{6}+20s^{5}-26s^{4}-85s^{3}-26s^{2}+20s+8}\; }.
\end{equation}
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}[Proof sketch (direct summation from the correlation generating function)]
By Corollary \ref{cor:fold-gauge-anomaly-cov-genfun}, the lag covariance generating function for \(k\ge 1\),
\(
C(z)=\sum_{k\ge 1}C_k z^k
\),
is rational.
Since \(C_{-k}=C_k\) and \(C_0=\mathrm{Var}(g_t)=20/81\) (Theorem \ref{thm:fold-gauge-anomaly-autocov-closed}),
\(
\mathcal S_g(\omega)=C_0+C(e^{i\omega})+C(e^{-i\omega})
\).
Substituting \(z=s\) and \(z=s^{-1}\) and performing algebraic simplification yields \eqref{eq:fold-gauge-anomaly-psd-rational}. \qed
\end{proof}
\begin{proposition}[Fourth-Order Recurrence for the Total Gauge Anomaly: Probability Generating Function Closed by a Fixed Characteristic Polynomial]\label{prop:fold-gauge-anomaly-mgf-order4-recurrence}
Let \(G_m:=\sum_{t=1}^{m} g_t\), and for \(u>0\) define the probability generating function
\[
M_m(u):=\mathbb E\!\left[u^{G_m}\right]
=\mathbb E\exp\!\bigl((\log u)\,G_m\bigr).
\]
Introduce the denominator-cleared counting-type generating function \(\widetilde M_m(u):=2^{m}M_m(u)\).
Then for all \(m\ge 0\), the sequence \(\bigl(\widetilde M_m(u)\bigr)_{m\ge 0}\) satisfies the fourth-order linear recurrence
\begin{equation}\label{eq:fold-gauge-anomaly-Mm-order4}
\boxed{\;
\widetilde M_{m+4}(u)=\widetilde M_{m+3}(u)+(2u+1)\widetilde M_{m+2}(u)+(u^{3}-2u)\widetilde M_{m+1}(u)-2u\,\widetilde M_m(u)\; }.
\end{equation}
Equivalently, \(\bigl(M_m(u)\bigr)\) satisfies the same fourth-order recurrence, but with coefficients rescaled by \(2^{-j}\) throughout (corresponding to the scale difference \(A_\theta=\tfrac12(2A_\theta)\)).
At \(u=1\), the characteristic factorization of this recurrence is
\(
(\mu-2)(\mu-1)(\mu+1)^2
\),
where the Jordan double root at \((\mu+1)^2\) corresponds to the alternating-phase residual of Theorem \ref{thm:fold-gauge-anomaly-A0-jordan},
thereby explaining the \(m2^{-m}\)-level oscillatory correction term appearing in finite-length statistics (Theorem \ref{thm:fold-gauge-anomaly-var-finite-closed}).
\end{proposition}
\begin{proof}[Proof sketch (Cayley--Hamilton)]
Let \(\theta=\log u\) and take the matrix \(A_\theta\) of Proposition \ref{prop:fold-gauge-anomaly-pressure}.
Set \(B_u:=2A_\theta\); its characteristic polynomial is precisely
\(
F(\mu,u)=\det(\mu I-B_u)
\),
whose explicit quartic form is given in Proposition \ref{prop:fold-gauge-anomaly-pressure}.
By the Cayley--Hamilton theorem, \(F(B_u,u)=0\).
For fixed \(u\), the counting-type generating function \(\widetilde M_m(u)\) can be written as the path weight sum of a finite-state transducer, equivalently as a linear functional applied to \(B_u^m\);
multiplying \(F(B_u,u)=0\) on both sides by the appropriate vectors and taking this linear functional yields \eqref{eq:fold-gauge-anomaly-Mm-order4}. \qed
\end{proof}
\begin{proposition}[Non-Asymptotic Chernoff Profile: Tail Probability Exponent Uniquely Determined by the Algebraic Pressure Function]\label{prop:fold-gauge-anomaly-chernoff-nonasymptotic}
Let the pressure function be \(P_G(\theta)=\log\rho(A_\theta)\) as in Proposition \ref{prop:fold-gauge-anomaly-pressure}, and let
\[
I(a)=\sup_{\theta\in\RR}\bigl(a\theta-P_G(\theta)\bigr)\qquad(a\in[0,1])
\]
be its Legendre--Fenchel transform (Proposition \ref{prop:fold-gauge-anomaly-ldp}).
Then for any \(a\in(0,1)\) there exist a constant \(C(a)>0\) and an integer \(r(a)\ge 0\) such that for all \(m\ge 1\),
\begin{equation}\label{eq:fold-gauge-anomaly-chernoff-two-sided}
\boxed{\;
\mathbb P\!\left(\frac{G_m}{m}\ge a\right)\le C(a)\,m^{r(a)}e^{-m I(a)},\qquad
\mathbb P\!\left(\frac{G_m}{m}\le a\right)\le C(a)\,m^{r(a)}e^{-m I(a)}.\;}
\end{equation}
The saddle-point parameter \(u(a)=e^{\theta(a)}\) can be uniquely determined from the feasible branch of the elimination certificate \(R(a,u)=0\) (Proposition \ref{prop:fold-gauge-anomaly-rate-curve-param}), so the exponential profile \(I(a)\) is an auditable ``algebraic--logarithmic'' object;
the polynomial prefactor \(m^{r(a)}\) arises solely from the Jordan defect of the finite-dimensional transfer operator (and can be taken as \(r(a)\le 3\) in this \(4\)-state interface).
\end{proposition}
\begin{proof}[Proof sketch (matrix Chernoff + finite-dimensional spectral decomposition)]
For any \(\theta\in\RR\), the Chernoff inequality gives
\(
\mathbb P(G_m\ge am)\le e^{-am\theta}\,\mathbb E e^{\theta G_m}
\);
and \(\mathbb E e^{\theta G_m}\) is a matrix element (or linear combination thereof) of the finite-dimensional weighted adjacency matrix \(A_\theta\), hence can be bounded via finite-dimensional spectral/Jordan decomposition as
\(
\mathbb E e^{\theta G_m}\le C(\theta)\,m^{r(\theta)}\rho(A_\theta)^m
\).
Optimizing over \(\theta\) gives the exponential term \(I(a)\), and the remaining constant and polynomial factors are absorbed into \(C(a),r(a)\). \qed
\end{proof}
\begin{theorem}[Strict Sign Law and Far-Field Saturation of the Gallavotti--Cohen Defect]\label{thm:fold-gauge-anomaly-gc-defect-sign}
Define the GC defect function
\[
\Delta(\theta):=P_G(\theta)-\theta-P_G(-\theta).
\]
Then:
\begin{enumerate}
  \item \(\Delta\) is an odd function, \(\Delta(0)=0\);
  \item Its linearized bias satisfies
  \begin{equation}\label{eq:fold-gauge-anomaly-gc-defect-slope}
  \boxed{\;
  \Delta'(0)=2P_G'(0)-1=2\cdot\frac49-1=-\frac19\;};
  \end{equation}
  \item Its far-field limit satisfies
  \begin{equation}\label{eq:fold-gauge-anomaly-gc-defect-saturation}
  \boxed{\;
  \lim_{\theta\to+\infty}\Delta(\theta)=-\log\varphi\;};
  \end{equation}
  \item The strict sign law holds:
  \begin{equation}\label{eq:fold-gauge-anomaly-gc-defect-sign}
  \boxed{\;
  \Delta(\theta)<0\ (\theta>0),\qquad \Delta(\theta)>0\ (\theta<0)\;}.
  \end{equation}
\end{enumerate}
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}[Proof sketch (auditable)]
(1) Direct computation from the definition gives \(\Delta(-\theta)=-\Delta(\theta)\).
(2) From \(\Delta'(\theta)=P_G'(\theta)-1+P_G'(-\theta)\) evaluated at \(\theta=0\), using the closed form \(P_G'(0)=4/9\) from Proposition \ref{prop:fold-gauge-anomaly-pressure}.
(3) By the endpoint closed forms of Proposition \ref{prop:fold-gauge-anomaly-ldp}: as \(\theta\to+\infty\), \(P_G(\theta)=\theta-\log 2+o(1)\) and \(P_G(-\theta)\to \log(\varphi/2)\), so \(\Delta(\theta)\to -\log\varphi\).
(4) For this minimal \(4\)-state interface, \(\Delta\) is strictly decreasing on \(\theta>0\) (equivalently \(\Delta'(\theta)<0\)), which can be verified by converting \(\Delta'(\theta)\) to an explicit expression on the algebraic branch via the algebraic parametrization of Proposition \ref{prop:fold-gauge-anomaly-rate-curve-param} and performing a sign audit; by \(\Delta(0)=0\), \(\Delta(\theta)<0\) for \(\theta>0\). The sign for \(\theta<0\) follows from the odd symmetry. \qed
\end{proof}
\begin{corollary}[Two-Constant Closure: \texorpdfstring{$\frac49$}{4/9} and \texorpdfstring{$\log\varphi$}{log phi} Lock the Same Defect Curve Locally and in the Far Field]\label{cor:fold-gauge-anomaly-two-constants-closure}
Under the notation of Theorem \ref{thm:fold-gauge-anomaly-gc-defect-sign}, \(\Delta'(0)=-\frac19\) and
\(\lim_{\theta\to+\infty}\Delta(\theta)=-\log\varphi\) constitute a pair of local--far-field gauge conditions:
they are respectively induced by the mean constant \(P_G'(0)=4/9\) and the endpoint exponent \(I(0)=\log(2/\varphi)\) (Proposition \ref{prop:fold-gauge-anomaly-ldp}).
Moreover, at the origin there is a strict third-order correction (all even-order terms cancel exactly):
\begin{equation}\label{eq:fold-gauge-anomaly-delta-taylor3}
\boxed{\;
\Delta(\theta)= -\frac{\theta}{9}\;-\;\frac{1174}{6561}\,\theta^{3}\;+\;O(\theta^{5})\qquad(\theta\to 0).}
\end{equation}
Therefore the ``non-self-dual'' fingerprint of \(\Delta\) goes beyond the third cumulant being nonzero: it is sealed by both the local slope and the far-field saturation value of a single-parameter defect curve simultaneously.
\end{corollary}
\begin{proof}
By Proposition \ref{prop:fold-gauge-anomaly-pressure}, the first three derivatives of \(P_G\) at \(\theta=0\) all have closed forms,
and \(P_G\) is a smooth function.
Expanding \(P_G(\theta)\) and \(P_G(-\theta)\) in Taylor series and substituting into \(\Delta(\theta)=P_G(\theta)-\theta-P_G(-\theta)\);
noting that even-order terms cancel and odd-order terms double, yields \eqref{eq:fold-gauge-anomaly-delta-taylor3}. \qed
\end{proof}
\begin{proposition}[Finite Index of the Folding Conditional Expectation: Maximal Fiber Multiplicity Gives the Logarithmic Scale of Worst-Case Information Loss]\label{prop:fold-condexp-index-maxfiber}
Fix resolution \(m\).
Using the notation of Section \ref{subsec:pom-max-fiber}, write the fiber multiplicity as
\(
d_m(x)=|\Fold_m^{-1}(x)|
\)
and the maximal multiplicity as
\(
D_m=\max_{x\in X_m} d_m(x)
\).
Take the finite-dimensional commutative algebra \(A_m=\CC^{\Omega_m}\) and its subalgebra \(B_m\subset A_m\) (functions pulled back from \(X_m\), i.e., fiber-constant functions),
and let \(E_m:A_m\to B_m\) be the conditional expectation given by uniform averaging over fibers.
Then the Pimsner--Popa index satisfies the strict equality
\begin{equation}\label{eq:fold-condexp-index-maxfiber}
\boxed{\;
\mathrm{Ind}(E_m)=D_m\; }.
\end{equation}
Moreover, by Theorem \ref{thm:dephys-index-max-relative-entropy-loss} (the extremal formula for relative entropy loss of finite index), one obtains the finite-dimensional discrete prototype:
\begin{equation}\label{eq:fold-condexp-index-entropy-loss}
\boxed{\;
\sup_{\rho,\sigma}\Bigl[D(\rho\|\sigma)-D(\rho\circ E_m\ \|\ \sigma\circ E_m)\Bigr]
=\log \mathrm{Ind}(E_m)=\log D_m.\;}
\end{equation}
\end{proposition}
\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
For any nonneg function \(f\in A_m\) and any \(a\in\Omega_m\), if \(x=\Fold_m(a)\) and \(d=d_m(x)\), then
\(
(E_m f)(a)=\frac1d\sum_{b\in\Fold_m^{-1}(x)} f(b)\ge \frac1d f(a)
\).
Therefore \(E_m(f)\ge D_m^{-1}f\), i.e., \(\mathrm{Ind}(E_m)\le D_m\).
Conversely, take some \(x_\star\) achieving the maximal multiplicity and a point \(a_\star\) in its fiber; let \(f=\mathbf 1_{\{a_\star\}}\).
Then on this fiber \(E_m f \equiv 1/D_m\), so if \(E_m(f)\ge \Lambda^{-1}f\) holds, one must have \(\Lambda\ge D_m\), hence \(\mathrm{Ind}(E_m)\ge D_m\).
Combining gives \(\mathrm{Ind}(E_m)=D_m\).
Equation \eqref{eq:fold-condexp-index-entropy-loss} follows directly from Theorem \ref{thm:dephys-index-max-relative-entropy-loss}. \qed
\end{proof}
\begin{corollary}[Saturation Criterion for Fiber Entropy Potential: Strict Gap Between Average Log-Multiplicity and Average Multiplicity]\label{cor:fold-fiber-entropy-saturation}
For any \(\pi\in\Delta(X_m)\), define the fiber entropy potential
\[
S_{\mathrm{fib}}(\pi):=\mathbb E_{\pi}[\log d_m(X)].
\]
Then the Jensen upper bound always holds:
\begin{equation}\label{eq:fold-fiber-entropy-jensen-gap}
\boxed{\;
S_{\mathrm{fib}}(\pi)\le \log\mathbb E_{\pi}[d_m(X)]\;}
\end{equation}
with equality if and only if \(d_m(X)\) is \(\pi\)-almost surely constant (i.e., all visible types carry the same fiber multiplicity).
In particular, for the uniform visible baseline \(\pi=\mathrm{Unif}(X_m)\), \(\mathbb E_{\pi}[d_m(X)]=|\Omega_m|/|X_m|=I_m\) (Definition \ref{def:pom-fold-index}), so
\[
\boxed{\;
\mathbb E_{\pi}[\log d_m(X)]\le \log\frac{|\Omega_m|}{|X_m|}=S_Z(m)\; }.
\]
\end{corollary}
\begin{proof}
By the concavity of the logarithm (Jensen's inequality), \eqref{eq:fold-fiber-entropy-jensen-gap} follows.
The equality condition is that \(d_m(X)\) is constant on the \(\pi\)-support.
The last part follows from
\(
\mathbb E_{\mathrm{Unif}(X_m)}[d_m(X)]=\frac{1}{|X_m|}\sum_{x\in X_m} d_m(x)=\frac{|\Omega_m|}{|X_m|}
\).
\qed
\end{proof}
\begin{proposition}[Auditable ``Spectral--Tomographic--Certificate'' Triangle: Power Spectrum and Fourth-Order Recurrence Jointly Lock the Minimum Identification Complexity]\label{prop:fold-gauge-anomaly-spectrum-tomography-certificate-triangle}
Suppose an observer can access only two types of finite data:
\begin{enumerate}
  \item[(i)] Samples of the power spectrum on a finite frequency grid \(\{\mathcal S_g(\omega_\ell)\}_{\ell=1}^{L}\);
  \item[(ii)] Finite-length generating function values \(\{M_m(u)\}_{m=0}^{N}\) for a fixed \(u\neq 1\) (where \(N\ge 3\)).
\end{enumerate}
Then:
\begin{enumerate}
  \item By Proposition \ref{prop:fold-gauge-anomaly-mgf-order4-recurrence}, the data \(\{M_m(u)\}_{m=0}^{N}\) must algebraically lie in the four-dimensional linear space generated by the fourth-order recurrence;
  any implementation claiming ``the same mechanism'' must satisfy this finite-data consistency constraint.
  \item By Theorem \ref{thm:fold-gauge-anomaly-psd-rational}, \(\mathcal S_g\) has a fixed rational pole structure;
  any mechanism substitution that alters the \( (-1/2)\) alternating mode or its Jordan residual (Theorem \ref{thm:fold-gauge-anomaly-A0-jordan}) will produce detectable deviation at finitely many frequency points.
  \item After combining both types of data, the minimum identification complexity is forced by ``order \(4\)'':
  any attempt to simultaneously fit (i)--(ii) with a linear state model of order \(<4\) will fail in a strictly algebraic sense (unable to simultaneously satisfy the fourth-order recurrence and the pole/Jordan constraints of the spectral rational form).
\end{enumerate}
Therefore, the minimum verifiable carrying dimension of the gauge anomaly mechanism is strictly locked at \(4\), and can be audited simultaneously via the dual-channel certificate of ``recurrence consistency + frequency-domain pole structure.''
\end{proposition}
